title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation
layout_note: A long classification branch fills the top band; at the n x 64 point features and the global feature, two dashed arrows drop into a segmentation branch in the lower right. The empty lower left holds two zoom-in panels for the input and feature transforms, tied to their boxes by dashed grey leader lines.
grouping: Two dotted rounded panels with tints: light blue for the classification network (italic title 'Classification Network' above its top-left) and light cream for the segmentation network (italic 'Segmentation Network' below its bottom-left). Rotated bold labels 'input points' and 'output scores' sit on the panel's left/right edges. The T-Net details sit in white dotted rounded boxes.
shapes_depth: Flat rectangles: per-point tensors are tall white boxes with rotated size labels (nx3, nx64, nx1024), widths growing with channel count; shared MLPs are three small rounded bars joined by a vertical line labelled 'shared'; max pool is an open chevron; the global feature is a thin grey bar; in the segmentation head the concatenated tensor is half white, half grey (n x 1088) to show local plus repeated global features.
proposed_highlight: No colour accent: the contribution is the structure itself (shared per-point MLPs, symmetric max pool to a bold-labelled 'global feature'), with the T-Net alignment blocks expanded as callouts below.
lesson: Draw per-point tensors as tall boxes with n x C size labels and the shared MLP as stacked bars joined by a 'shared' line, so weight sharing across points and the max-pool bottleneck read from the shapes alone.
notes: venue = arXiv (remembered venue: CVPR 2017; not printed on the arXiv first page); year = arXiv preprint year. Grey fill in the segmentation tensor marks the copied global feature.

arrangement.units: top lane: light-blue dotted rounded panel with the classification network; bottom-right: light-cream dotted rounded panel with the segmentation head; bottom-left: two white dotted boxes detailing the input and feature transforms
arrangement.inputs_as: a white n x 3 tensor box with a rotated bold 'input points' label on the panel edge; no point-cloud drawing
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; outputs are 'output scores' boxes (k for classification at the top right, n x m at the segmentation panel's right edge)
arrangement.shared: the segmentation branch reuses the classification trunk: dashed arrows bring the n x 64 local features and the 1024 global feature down into the segmentation panel

taxonomy.task: point cloud classification and part/semantic segmentation
taxonomy.note: multi-stream: a classification trunk with a segmentation branch that reuses its local and global features; plug-in-module: the T-Net alignment blocks

insights.structure: A full-width tinted classification lane on top, a tinted segmentation panel below it on the right, and the two T-Net detail callouts filling the empty lower left.
insights.data: Tensors are white rectangles whose widths grow with channels and carry rotated n x C labels, the global feature is a thin grey bar, and the segmentation input is a white-plus-grey block showing local and global parts concatenated.
insights.emphasis: Bold labels mark 'global feature', 'point features' and the 'output scores', and 'shared' sits on every per-point MLP so the key invariance trick is repeated in place.
insights.flow: Left to right along the top lane through transform, shared MLPs and max pool; two dashed arrows then drop down into the segmentation panel, which reads left to right to the n x m scores.
insights.avoid: The figure has no data thumbnails, so a reader never sees a point cloud, and the many small numeric labels (mlp (64,128,1024), 512,256,k) crowd the top lane.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
